original_question: Does there exist a maximal curve over the finite field F_{27^2} whose Frobenius dimension is 3 and whose Frobenius linear series has D-order sequence (0, 1, 3, 27)? Equivalently, can case (A) occur for a maximal curve with Frobenius dimension 3, namely the case in which the second generic D-order satisfies epsilon_2 = 3?
target_in_paper: Conjecture 1.1 in Section 1 of the paper, as sharpened by Proposition 1.2 and answered affirmatively by Theorem 1.3: the existence of an F_{q^2}-maximal curve of Frobenius dimension 3 whose Frobenius linear series has generic D-order sequence (0,1,3,q), realized in the paper for q = 27.
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the paper’s target as the unresolved case for maximal curves with Frobenius dimension 3, namely the existence question for the generic D-order sequence (0,1,3,q). It also correctly specializes to q = 27, matches the paper’s case-(A) language via epsilon_2 = 3, and uses the right ambient finite field F_{27^2}.
missing_details: The curve should be specified as a projective, nonsingular, geometrically irreducible algebraic curve X defined over F_{27^2}.
The Frobenius linear series should be defined as D = |(q+1)P_0| with q = 27 and P_0 any F_{27^2}-rational point of X.
“Frobenius dimension 3” should be stated as dim(D) = 3.
The sequence (0,1,3,27) is the generic D-order sequence (epsilon_0, epsilon_1, epsilon_2, epsilon_3), not merely a local order sequence at a special point.
If one uses the alternate wording, case (A) should be identified exactly as in Proposition 1.2: the branch where epsilon_2 = 3.
refined_question: Does there exist a projective, nonsingular, geometrically irreducible F_{27^2}-maximal curve X such that, for its Frobenius linear series D = |(27+1)P_0| with P_0 in X(F_{27^2}), one has dim(D) = 3 and generic D-order sequence (epsilon_0, epsilon_1, epsilon_2, epsilon_3) = (0,1,3,27)?
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently, in the setting of Proposition 1.2 for F_{q^2}-maximal curves of Frobenius dimension 3, can case (A) occur; that is, can the second generic D-order satisfy epsilon_2 = 3 (and in particular for q = 27)?
justification: Section 1 introduces the Frobenius linear series D = |(q+1)P_0| for an F_{q^2}-maximal curve X and defines its projective dimension r as the Frobenius dimension. In the Frobenius-dimension-3 case, the paper states that epsilon_0 = 0, epsilon_1 = 1, and epsilon_3 = q are already known, so the unresolved issue is precisely the value of epsilon_2. Conjecture 1.1 formulates the existence of a maximal curve with generic D-order sequence (0,1,3,q). Proposition 1.2 recasts the unresolved situation into alternatives and identifies the desired one as case (A), namely epsilon_2 = 3. Theorem 1.3 then settles this by proving existence for q = 27. So your draft is already very close, but to be fully stand-alone and paper-faithful it should explicitly define X, maximality, D, dim(D), and the fact that (0,1,3,27) is the generic D-order sequence.
